title: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security
summary: This research paper introduces a co-evolutionary framework where LLM code agents autonomously edit repositories to reproduce real exploits in isolated containers. The study demonstrates automated offensive capabilities using execution-verified rewards.

title: Coordinated Retrieval Poisoning Attacks Against RAG Systems
summary: Researchers investigated retrieval poisoning attacks in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, demonstrating how injected passages consistently reach top retrieval results. The work evaluates the success of these poisoning campaigns against existing defense mechanisms.

title: Information Injection Attacks Against LLM Financial Trading Agents
summary: Researchers demonstrated that LLM financial trading agents are vulnerable to fabricated news feeds designed to manipulate trading behavior. The benchmark shows how malicious headlines can steer autonomous agents into coordinated financial transactions.

sources.title: Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents

title: One-Relation Attack: Manipulating LLM Agents via Inferential Warrants
summary: Researchers introduced the one-relation attack, demonstrating that a single targeted sentence can mislead LLM agents and alter their reasoning outcomes. Evaluations across eighteen models showed successful manipulation in biomedical inference and vulnerability tasks.

sources.title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents

title: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Researchers introduced RAGLeak, a supply-chain privacy backdoor attack that extracts sensitive data from retrieval-augmented generation systems. The technique balances extraction fidelity and stealthiness better than previous prompt injection or backdoor methods.

sources.title: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

title: Decision Dynamics of LLM Agents Following Prompt Injections
summary: Researchers used branching rollouts to analyze when and why LLM agents decide to follow prompt injections embedded in untrusted content. The findings challenge assumptions that compliance with injections is strictly determined at the moment of reading.

sources.title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections

title: Safeguard Measurements and Vulnerabilities in Options-Trading LLM Agents
summary: A security measurement of shipped options-trading LLM agents across multiple repositories and broker documentation revealed significant lack of safeguards. The study highlights risks where automated order paths can reach unbounded financial losses.

title: Trojan-Based Data Poisoning Attacks Increasing LLM Token Response Costs
summary: Researchers devised a defense against a data-poisoning attack that plants a Trojan to artificially increase LLM response lengths and financial costs. The attack triggers on semantically similar instructions within prompts.

title: Dormant Poisoning Attacks and Agentic Risks Across Fine-Tuned Models

title: SEAL: Persistent Tool Poisoning Attack against LLM Agents
